Urgent medical matters during weekdays? Call your general practitioner (GP). Urgent medical matters during evenings, nights, weekends or public holidays? Call the out-of-hours service (huisartsen-spoedpost). You can find the number for the out-of-hours service on your GP practice's website. Or on your GP's answering machine. In case of a life-threatening emergency: call 112 In case of a life-threatening emergency: call 112 In case of a life-threatening emergency: call 112. This number is available 24 hours a day and will give you access to all emergency services: ambulance, police and fire brigade. In a medical emergency, you will also be instructed what to do until the ambulance arrives. Urgent medical matters during weekdays: call your general practitioner (GP) Urgent medical matters during weekdays: call your general practitioner (GP) For other, non-life-threatening, medical emergencies during office hours, first call your GP. You can call your GP between 8 o'clock in the morning and 5 o'clock in the afternoon on weekdays. The GP practice will have a separate emergency number or a voice response system that will give you immediate access to your care provider. Often you can also find the emergency phone number on your doctor's website. You will usually speak to the GP assistant first, and then the GP if necessary. For urgent matters, the GP will visit you at home immediately if necessary. If you need to go to hospital, the GP will call the ambulance and the specialist at the hospital who will take over your medical care. Urgent medical matters during evenings, nights, weekends or public holidays: out-of-hours service (huisartsen-spoedpost) Urgent medical matters during evenings, nights, weekends or public holidays: out-of-hours service (huisartsen-spoedpost) When the GP practice is closed, you can call the out-of-hours service for medical emergencies. This means: on weekdays between 5 o'clock in the afternoon and 8 o'clock in the morning and on weekend days and public holidays. The out-of-hours service ( huisartsen-spoedpost in Dutch) is a central office where GPs are available on call. If you call your GP's practice out of hours, their answering machine will tell you (often in Dutch) which phone numbers you can call for GP care and in case of emergencies. You can also usually find the number for the out-of-hours service on your GP practice's website. Or search for it on the internet. Type in your search engine: huisartsen-spoedpost, and then the name of the place where you live. You can call the out-of-hours service. But often, you can also email or chat. Sometimes you first have to fill out a questionnaire and then speak to the assistant if necessary. When you call the out-of-hours service, you will speak to a specially trained GP assistant. The assistant will ask you your name, date of birth and health insurance details, after which you explain what the problem is. The assistant will ask you questions to determine how serious your situation is. Sometimes discussing your problem with the assistant and getting advice or medication is enough. Sometimes the GP on duty will need to call you back. In other cases, you will get an appointment to see a GP at the out-of-hours service. In some cases it is necessary for the GP to visit you at home. This subtitled video tells you more about the out-of-hours service. Mental health crisis: GP or out-of-hours service Mental health crisis: GP or out-of-hours service If you or someone you know is experiencing a mental health crisis, contact your general practitioner (GP) or the out-of-hours service ( huisartsen-spoedpost ) immediately. If necessary, the GP can contact the local Crisis Intervention Team (available 24/7). If you or someone you know has suicidal thoughts, you can also call 0800-0113 or 113, an anonymous helpline .
